dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that estimates the power spectral density of a random process two ways and overlays the closed-form S(omega): an averaged periodogram (Welch with Hann windows and 50% overlap, or Bartlett with rectangular segments) and the Wiener-Khinchin route, the Fourier transform of the biased sample autocorrelation tapered by a lag window matched to the segment window. Processes are white noise, AR(1), a moving average of length q, and a sinusoid in noise, all driven by seeded white noise. Read-outs give the RMS dB difference between the two estimates and each one's RMS error against theory; with one rectangular segment the two estimates are identical.
relation: Chapter 12: Stochastic Processes and Random Signals

searchKeywords: PSD is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation
periodogram equals FT of sample autocorrelation

topic: Variance and resolution of spectral estimates
learningObjectives: Explain the Wiener-Khinchin theorem and verify that the periodogram of one rectangular segment equals the Fourier transform of the biased sample autocorrelation
Calculate r[k], S(0) and S(pi) for AR(1) and moving-average processes from their closed forms
Analyze how the number of averaged segments K trades variance against frequency resolution, using the RMS error against theory and the depth of the moving-average nulls
Relate features of an autocorrelation (decay rate, alternating sign, finite length, a component that never decays) to features of the PSD
Distinguish agreement between two estimates from accuracy against the true PSD
prerequisites: Mean, variance and autocorrelation of a wide-sense stationary process

misconceptions.misconception: A longer record gives a more accurate periodogram
misconceptions.correction: Each periodogram value keeps a standard deviation about equal to its mean however long the record is; only averaging segments (or lag windowing) reduces the variance
misconceptions.evidence: With Bartlett and K = 1 the RMS error against theory stays between 5.4 and 6.4 dB for N = 64 to 4096, while Welch with N = 4096 and K = 63 reaches 0.57 dB

misconceptions.misconception: If two PSD estimates agree, they are correct
misconceptions.correction: Both estimates are computed from the same record and share its errors; their agreement demonstrates the Wiener-Khinchin identity, not accuracy
misconceptions.evidence: With Bartlett and K = 1 the two estimates differ by 0.00 dB, yet each is 6.35 dB RMS from the true PSD

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Three stacked plots estimate the power spectral density of a random process. Top: the first samples of one realization x[n], with the analysis segments in gold. Middle: the sample autocorrelation r-hat[k] for lags -32 to 32 (blue stems), the theoretical autocorrelation (black rings) and the lag window (gold). Bottom: the PSD in dB from 0 to pi radians per sample, estimated by an averaged periodogram (maroon) and by the Fourier transform of r-hat[k] (green, the Wiener-Khinchin theorem), with the theoretical S(omega) dashed in black. Read-outs give the RMS difference between the two estimates and their errors against theory. Controls choose the process, its parameter, the record length N, the number of averaged segments K, the window method and the random seed.

controls.label: Process
controls.description: Chooses the random process; all are driven by the same seeded unit-variance white noise

controls.label: Method
controls.description: Chooses the averaged periodogram: Welch (Hann windows, 50% overlap) or Bartlett (rectangular windows, no overlap); the lag window of the Wiener-Khinchin estimate follows the choice

controls.label: Process parameter (a, q or omega_0)
controls.description: AR coefficient a from -0.95 to 0.95 (step 0.05, default 0.90); MA length q from 1 to 32 (default 8); sinusoid frequency omega_0 from 0.05 pi to 0.95 pi (step 0.01 pi, default 0.25 pi); disabled for white noise

controls.label: Record length N
controls.description: Sets the record length N = 2^value, from 64 to 4096 samples

controls.label: Averages K
controls.description: Sets the number of averaged segments K; the segment length is M = floor(N/K) (Bartlett) or floor(2N/(K+1)) (Welch), and K is capped so that M is at least 16

controls.label: New realization
controls.description: Advances the random seed by one and draws new white noise

controls.label: Reset seed
controls.description: Returns to seed 1 so that results can be reproduced and compared

visualElements.description: Realization x[n] (first 512 samples, blue) with the Hann windows or rectangular segments in gold
Biased sample autocorrelation r-hat[k] for |k| <= 32 (blue stems), theoretical r[k] (black rings) and lag window c[k] (gold dashed); hovering a lag prints r-hat[k] and r[k]

PSD in dB for 0 to pi: averaged periodogram (maroon band), Fourier transform of c[k] r-hat[k] (green), theory (black dashed) and, for the sinusoid, an arrow for the spectral line; hovering a frequency prints the three values
RMS and maximum dB difference between the two estimates, and each estimate's RMS dB error against theory

model.description: Generates N samples of a zero-mean process from seeded Gaussian white noise (Box-Muller), computes the biased sample autocorrelation with an FFT, the averaged periodogram of K windowed segments of M samples, and the lag-windowed Fourier transform of the sample autocorrelation, all on an FFT grid of at least 1024 points, and compares them in dB with the closed-form PSD
equations: MA(q): r[k] = sigma^2 (1 - |k|/q) for |k| < q, S(w) = sigma^2 sin^2(qw/2) / (q sin^2(w/2))
S_avg(w) = (1/K) sum_i |sum_n v[n] x[n + iD] e^{-jwn}|^2 / sum_n v[n]^2
algorithms: Seeded PRNG (mulberry32) with the Box-Muller transform

instructionalStrategies: Verify the periodogram identity with one rectangular segment before averaging
Step K and record the RMS error against theory to see the variance-resolution trade-off
Predict the PSD shape from the autocorrelation before reading it
extensions: Add an AR(2) process with a resonant peak
Add a parametric (Yule-Walker) estimate as a third route to the PSD
